newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia late olein stable, sellers retreat.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia late olein stable, sellers retreat.

text.p: Indonesian palm olein prices were stable in late trading on Monday with many sellers retreating following hefty gains in Malaysia, traders said.
They said olein remained at 1,425-30 rupiah/kg in Jakarta, but sellers who were offering below the range in the morning session started hiking values.

"Players who were selling cheap began raising prices while others pulled out of the market," one trader said. "Sellers are expecting local prices to increase tomorrow. Prices may open at 1,440 rupiah (on Tuesday)." Malaysian values rose sharply following the release of supportive crop data on Monday.
Cargo surveyor, Societe Generale de Surveillance (SGS) said it estimated Malaysian palm oil exports for December 1-15 at 406,924 tonnes, compared with 298,862 tonnes for the same November period.

Earlier in the day, Malaysia's Palm Oil Registration and Licensing Authority (PORLA) said in a report the country's crude palm oil production fell 13.83 percent to 762,540 tonnes in November from 743,251 tonnes in October.
PORLA said Malaysia's palm oil stocks rose 0.12 percent to 955,965 tonnes at end-November from 954,841 tonnes end-October.
